findings.text: Releases contiguous device memory by preferring a device private area when present, otherwise trying shared areas, and finally returning pages to the general allocator when no shared area accepts them.

Reports currently tracked mappings to the kernel log, optionally narrowed to one device, including type, index, physical and device addresses, length, cacheline number, direction, error check state and attributes.
Indicates whether bounce buffering is available for a device by checking for an attached buffer pool with a nonzero extent.

Tracking record holds linkage, owning device, device address, length, mapping category, transfer direction, scatter counts for requested and mapped extents, physical address, error check state, attribute flags, plus optional call trace storage, with cacheline alignment on multiprocessor builds.
Hash storage pairs a linkage list with interrupt safe spin protection; the global table holds many such buckets indexed by device address.
Hash geometry uses 16384 buckets, a shift of 13 and a mask equal to bucket count minus one.

Initial tracking pool holds 65536 entries, with an initial count variable set to that value, while dynamic growth allocates one page worth of records at a time and updates free, minimum free and total counters.
Stored call trace depth is 5 entries and driver name filtering uses a 64 character buffer.

Mapping categories distinguish single, scatter gather, coherent, noncoherent and physical memory uses; error check states distinguish not applicable, unchecked and checked; direction labels cover bidirectional, to device, from device and none.
Overlap ceiling corresponds to all tag bits set; per page cacheline geometry derives from page shift minus level one cache shift, with a count of one shifted by that difference.
Release accounting rounds the requested length up to page granularity before deriving the page count.
Bucket selection shifts the recorded device address right by the hash shift and masks to table size, emphasizing middle address bits.
Exact lookup requires same owning device and same device address; containing lookup requires same device plus full enclosure of the reference extent by the candidate extent.

Bucket search scores candidates on agreement of length, category, direction and requested scatter count, returning immediately on full agreement, otherwise remembering the highest score and succeeding only when exactly one candidate matched.

Containing search probes successive earlier buckets by decrementing the address by one hash quantum, bounded by the smaller of table size and address derived limit, releasing each bucket before acquiring the previous one.

Reserved memory nodes qualify only when marked reusable and not marked no map; a default designated node is refused when a command line size override is active, with distinct negative codes for ineligible versus overridden cases.
Validation raises the required alignment to at least the minimum contiguous alignment; setup rejects regions whose base or size combination is misaligned and reports setup failures distinctly.
Device attachment stores the reserved area private pointer into the device structure and detachment clears it.

Cacheline identity combines the physical page number scaled by cachelines per page with the in page offset scaled by level one line size; transfers toward the device bypass both insertion and removal.

Overlap concern is suppressed when the new mapping carries a skip synchronization flag, or when both the new and existing mappings carry cacheline exempt or coherent required attributes, subject to alignment and bounce buffering conditions.

Each hash bucket has its own interrupt safe spin protection acquired on lookup or insertion and released afterwards; containing search holds at most one bucket at a time across its backward walk, and dump paths hold each bucket only while scanning its list.
A dedicated spin lock guards the free record list and its counters during allocation, dynamic growth and release, with allocation using interrupt safe save and restore.
A dedicated spin lock guards active cacheline tree mutations and overlap tag updates during insertion and removal, using interrupt safe save and restore.
A reader writer lock guards comparison of the configured driver filter string and lazy binding of the filter to a driver object, using interrupt safe reader acquisition.

Free pool grows by page sized batches when empty under atomic allocation, tracks totals and low water mark, emits a notice each time growth crosses a multiple of the initial pool size, and returns released records to the head for cache warmth.

Debug activity is suppressed when globally disabled or not yet initialized; otherwise each error increments a global counter, prints subject to driver filtering and either unrestricted or limited remaining budget, decrements the limited budget when used, and optionally appends a stored trace.
Filtering is inactive with an empty configured name; once configured it accepts only matching devices, rejects missing devices, and latches the first matching driver object for later fast acceptance.

Reserved memory handling dispatches validation, fixup, setup and device bind or unbind through a constant operation table, with early phases verifying eligibility and setup publishing the created area as default when so designated and recording it for later insertion.

Overlap state reads tag bits as a count, writes counts back to tags with range validation, increments on duplicate insertion with a one time warning on overflow for non exempt entries, decrements on removal and deletes the tree node when the count drops below zero.
Sequential output iterates every bucket under per bucket protection and formats each record with driver, device, type, index, addresses, length, cacheline, direction, error state and attributes.

Recording appends the new entry to its bucket then performs cacheline insertion, disabling further debugging on resource exhaustion and reporting unsupported overlaps when exemption and platform conditions do not apply.
Exhaustion during dynamic growth, cacheline resource failure or similar resource pressure permanently disables debugging via a global flag to avoid unreliable tracking.

Duplicate physical mappings without hardware translation can alias to the same device addresses, so best fit selection and exempt attributes exist to reduce false overlap reports while still warning on genuine unsupported sharing.
